characteristics.cultivar: Bai Ye No. 1 (natural temperature-sensitive albino mutant)
characteristics.roast: None (pan fixation and gentle drying only)
characteristics.harvestSeason: Very early spring (leaves are pale albino only during the first cold weeks of spring)

description.short: Despite its name ('White Tea'), this is a green tea made from a rare albino cultivar — extraordinarily sweet, tender, and rich in L-theanine
description.overview: The name can be misleading: processed via pan fixation without fermentation, it is classified as a green tea. It is called 'white tea' because of the pale, almost translucent ivory-white leaves of its cold-sensitive albino mutant cultivar.
description.leaf: Slender, straight, pale jade to translucent yellow-white shoots with contrasting dark green central veins
description.liquor: Extremely pale, bright, almost translucent yellow-green liquor
description.aroma: Delicate, sweet, with fresh bamboo and chestnut undertones
description.taste: Exceptionally sweet and savory-umami due to extraordinarily high amino acid levels (up to double standard green teas, particularly L-theanine), with virtually no bitterness
description.processing: Plucking during a brief spring window while leaves remain albino (they turn ordinary green as weather warms) → pan fixation → gentle shaping → drying

history.origin: A single wild mother bush carrying this genetic chlorophyll mutation was discovered in the Anji mountains in the 1930s, remaining a botanical curiosity for decades
history.development: Asexual propagation via cuttings began in the 1980s when agricultural scientists and local authorities recognized its extraordinary potential
history.modern: Today, Anji Baicha is one of China's most coveted premium green teas, renowned for its umami richness and record-high amino acid content
interestingFacts: The leaves express their albino trait only when temperatures remain below approximately 23°C; as spring warms up, new flushes revert to ordinary green, strictly limiting the harvest window to 2–3 weeks
Despite containing the character 'Bai' (White), it is technically a classic green tea processed with shaqing fixation rather than a withered white tea, a frequent point of confusion for beginners
